descriptionChirho: The proper noun Canaan, referring either to the grandson of Noah (son of Ham) or to the geographic territory of the land of Canaan promised to Israel; consistently transliterated across languages as Canaán/Kenaan (Spa), कनान (Hin), كَنْعَان (Arb), 가나안 (Kor), Kanaani (Swa). Both bare and conjunction-prefixed forms carry identical referential semantics pointing to either the ancestor or the land named after him.

A secondary, metonymic usage where 'Canaan' functions as a common noun meaning 'merchant' or 'trader,' reflecting the ancient association of Canaanites/Phoenicians with commerce; the English gloss 'a merchant' and the Swahili mfanyabiashara ('one who does business') diverge sharply from the standard proper-noun transliterations, revealing a genuine semantic shift from ethnonym to occupational descriptor, paralleled in Hosea 12:8 and Ezekiel 17:4.
